title: Prospective surveillance study of acute respiratory infections, influenza-like illness and seasonal influenza vaccine in a cohort of juvenile idiopathic arthritis patients.
ehr_evidence: Routine clinical evaluations, including the Pediatric American College of Rheumatology 30% ( ACRPed30) were conducted during both surveillance periods prior to and at 30, 90 and 180 days after influenza vaccination.
summary: Prospective surveillance study evaluating the frequency and impact of acute respiratory infections and influenza-like illness on juvenile idiopathic arthritis disease activity, and assessing the immunogenicity and safety of the influenza vaccine in JIA patients.
key_findings: 105 ARI episodes were reported, with 26.6% classified as ILI.
60% of 33 respiratory samples were positive for at least one virus, with influenza and rhinovirus detected in 30% of samples.
20% of 50 observed JIA flares were temporally associated with ARI episodes.
Influenza seroprotection rates exceeded 70% (91-100%) and seroconversion rates exceeded 40% (74-93%).
Patients using anti-TNF alpha drugs presented lower seroconversion to the H1N1 strain (p=0.03).
No significant differences were found in ACRPed30 scores after vaccination (p=0.22).
No patient reported ILI symptoms during the 6-month post-vaccination follow-up period.
population: children and adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), mean age 10.7-11.0 years, Brazil
exposure_domain: respiratory viral infections and influenza vaccination
limitations: observational design limits causal inference between ARI and JIA flares
potential confounding by seasonality and immunosuppressive therapy
lack of statistical power to adjust for all covariates
